static_axes.branch_predicates_and_fallthroughs: All target/fallthrough edges, common joins, unknown-type handling, and both returns are recorded above. Type order is -1, 0x8000, 0, then 3; every other loaded type releases and returns 1.

static_axes.backend_pointer_contract: The registered slots are g_9140 at DGROUP:0x9140 (four-coordinate far function pointer returning screen-area byte size) and g_9148 at DGROUP:0x9148 (four coordinates plus far output buffer). Their actual call-site stack layouts are recorded by original code. Production m1CE2.c uses both with these signatures; m1B73.asm independently shows the g_9148 rectangle-plus-far-buffer stack order. Test aliases f_0250_0721/f_0250_0D10 are synthetic adapters only and are not represented as production targets.
static_axes.pointer_and_decoder_boundaries: The three original decoder callees are S03:3258:040D, S01:32B5:000F, S00:35A6:0007. Their source/disassembly homes confirm source far pointer at BP+6, destination far pointer at BP+0A, shift at BP+0E, flag at BP+10. The caller passes picture+8, scratch h, branch-specific x shift, and zero in this order. The two f_1B4E callees take x,y,far image at BP+6/+8/+0A.
static_axes.state_and_side_effects: The only target global decision state is g_5A97; backend pointer slots are read to make the two indirect calls. Target itself writes only scratch sentinel h[n]; resource, scratch, decoder, and draw effects are delegated through the same call boundaries/arguments/order as original. No target global or input picture write was found.
static_axes.numeric_and_layout: Pic fields are at offsets 0,2,8,10 under the declared 2-byte DOS layout; original accesses those exact offsets and widths. All masks, additions, byte/word loads, wrap points, sentinel, format strings, and decoder arguments are enumerated above.
static_axes.dependency_boundaries: GPutPacked and f_1B4E calls reach the production helper sources; type-3 decoder bodies are original symbolic assembly and were checked by context.py. DB, allocator, diagnostic, and graphics services remain external dependencies but their call ABI, data arguments, and ordering are identical at this function boundary.

limits: The suite is finite and is corroboration only; static CFG/dataflow/call comparison above supplies the completeness argument. The run records compiled_source_sha256 46f67c80... and registered source_sha256 c4329ddb...; the function bodies were compared and are text-identical, but the whole-module source identities differ.

The suite maps the registered g_9140/g_9148 slots to synthetic size/readback adapters and uses a virtual screen. It checks target geometry, the complete modeled scratch buffer, decoder output and call order, but it does not run a physical framebuffer or prove display-driver integration.

The test stubs GPutPacked and f_1B4E draw effects to logical request/pointer projections; this does not hide a caller mismatch because original and candidate call the same production dependency boundaries with the same arguments. Actual target helper implementations are outside this function-level receipt.

The g_9140 return-type spelling differs between m259D.c (unsigned int) and m1CE2.c (int); this target passes/stores the returned 16-bit AX bits as unsigned size and performs no signed size comparison.
No registry or canonical source was modified. This receipt is for independent root review only.

review_notes: Full static comparison found no semantic gap in win_DrawBitMap's own algorithm, conditions, constants, pointer arithmetic, state reads, or call sequence.

The production backend function pointers are runtime values in registered DGROUP slots; this audit proves the caller-side ABI, inputs, output-buffer pointer, and call order against the original and production call-site sources, not the behavior of every possible display driver target.
No claim is made that the finite virtual-screen differential is physical backend integration or universal input proof.

The C source is a partial historical byte reconstruction (scaffold marker and strict 675-vs-663 mismatch); BEHAVIOR_EXACT_CONFIRMED here concerns static function semantics only, not historical object acceptance. The existing differential's compiled source is an earlier seed with the same function body text, so it is corroborating evidence rather than proof that the current whole module was compiled and run.

root_review.basis: Reviewed the whole-function branch/call/state/width maps, source/evidence identities, explanations of residue and differential/negative limits. Matching observed service boundaries are composed through the actual caller ABI and same callee/slot/state; finite coverage alone is not acceptance.
